newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Seguin hints may be time to drop Juppe.
newsitem.headline: France's Seguin hints may be time to drop Juppe.

text.p: French parliamentary speaker Philippe Seguin, a heavyweight critic of Prime Minister Alain Juppe within his Gaullist RPR party, indicated on Monday that it may be time to change premiers given Sunday's election warning.

"You don't change campaign leaders in the middle of the watch, but given that one of the best hypotheses is that the centre-right could win a majority of a few seats (in the second round), the problems at stake are different from those posed by a hundred-seat advance," Seguin told RTL radio.
"My forecast, and it has always been the same, is that the margin will be of five or six seats," said Seguin, speaker of the National Assembly.

"The centre-right still has all its chances of having a five to six-seat lead provided that it clearly makes known the answers it will give to the message which has been delivered (by voters)," Seguin added.

Voters gave the combined left a 4.5-point lead over the centre-right coalition in the first round of a general election and raised the prospect that Gaullist President Jacques Chirac may have to share power with the Socialist-led bloc after next Sunday's runoff ballot.
